Step 1 – Grignard addition  
trans-cinnamaldehyde Ph-CH=CH-CHO (9 C)  
+ MeMgBr  ⟶  Ph-CH=CH-CH(OH)-CH3  
The methyl of the Grignard reagent adds to the carbonyl carbon, so one carbon is gained.  
Product 1: 9 + 1 = 10 carbons.

Step 2 – PCC oxidation  
Ph-CH=CH-CH(OH)-CH3  ⟶  Ph-CH=CH-CO-CH3  
Only oxidation of the secondary alcohol to a ketone; no atoms are added or removed.  
Product 2: still 10 carbons.

Step 3 – Corey–Chaykovsky reaction  
The sulfoxonium ylide (dimethyl(oxo)-λ6-sulfaneylidene)methane, ≡ ⁻CH2–S⁺(Me)2O, reacts with the ketone carbonyl of product 2.  
• The ylide’s carbanion adds to the carbonyl carbon.  
• Intramolecular displacement of DMSO closes an epoxide ring.  
• The CH2 carbon of the ylide becomes the second carbon of the new oxirane ring.  

Thus exactly one additional carbon is incorporated in this step.  
Product 3 therefore contains 10 + 1 = 11 carbon atoms.

Hence the total number of carbons in product 3 is 11.

Answer: A
